Write a Distribution in Different Coordinates

Source: R/reparametrize.R
reparametrize.Rd

Returns the same law as distrib, parametrized by quantities of the caller's choosing.

The function is meant for trying a parametrization that the package does not ship. Every derivative that it returns is assembled from the parent's derivatives through the map, one order at a time, so it costs more than a family written for that parametrization; a parametrization used in a real analysis is better written as a distribution of its own, with its derivatives in compiled code, which is how the families of this package are written.

Usage

reparametrize(
  distrib,
  map,
  params,
  bounds,
  links,
  map_derivs = NULL,
  interpretation = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  params_smooth = NULL
)

Arguments

distrib

The distribution to rewrite.

map

A function of a named list of the new parameters, returning a named list of the parent's.

params

A character vector naming the new parameters.

bounds

A named list of length-two numeric vectors, the open interval in which each new parameter lies.

links

A named list of linkfunctions7 links, one per new parameter.

map_derivs

An optional function of two arguments, the named list of new parameters and order, an integer from 1 to 4, returning for each parent parameter the non-zero partial derivatives of the map with respect to the new parameters up to order order, keyed by the sorted tuple of new-parameter positions ("1", "1,2", "2,2,3,3", ...); a missing key is an exact zero. Each caller passes the highest order that it reads, so a gradient passes order one and a fourth derivative passes order four. The shipped second parametrizations supply hand-written tables (see reparam_map_derivs()); when map_derivs is NULL, each needed partial comes from one finite-difference stencil on the map.

interpretation

An optional named character vector describing each new parameter; defaults to the parameter names.

name

An optional name for the result; defaults to the parent's with the new parameters appended.

params_smooth

An optional named logical vector with one entry per new parameter. An entry is TRUE when the log-density is differentiable in that new parameter. Because the map is arbitrary, the default cannot identify which new parameter reaches a kink of the parent: it is TRUE for every new parameter when every parameter of the parent is smooth, and FALSE for every one otherwise.

Value

A distribution object of class ReparamContinuousDistrib() or ReparamDiscreteDistrib().

Details

A link changes the scale on which a parameter is modeled and leaves the parameter itself unchanged. In a reparametrization the parameter is the new quantity, and the estimate, the standard error and the confidence interval describe that quantity.

The map is written in ordinary R. It takes a named list of the new parameters and returns a named list of the parent's, and it does not mention derivatives:


function(psi) list(mu = psi$mean / gamma(1 + 1 / psi$sigma),
                   sigma = psi$sigma)

The map's derivatives come from one of two routes, and map_derivs selects between them. If map_derivs is supplied, the tables are hand-written closed forms, exact at every order and written without a transcribed chain rule; the shipped second parametrizations all supply it, and their formulas are in reparam_map_derivs(). If map_derivs is NULL, each partial that the chain needs comes from one central stencil of numericals7::fd_derivative() applied to the analytic map, a single stencil per order and never a chain of differences. The stencil route is accurate to about \(10^{-11}\) at first order and loses accuracy quickly with the order (the third and fourth tables can be wrong in their leading digits), so a family used for anything beyond a first exploration needs map_derivs.

The derivatives of the log-density are carried by $$\ell^{(I)}(\psi) = \sum_{\pi} \sum_{i_1 \dots i_{|\pi|}} \ell^{(i_1 \dots i_{|\pi|})}(\theta) \prod_{B \in \pi} \frac{\partial^{|B|}\theta_{i_B}}{\partial \psi_B},$$ the sum over set partitions, so every order that the parent has in closed form survives in closed form. Because expectation is linear and the map is deterministic, the expected derivatives obey the same formula, and the term that carries the parent's score (multiplied by a derivative of the map of the order being formed) drops because the score has mean zero: a parent with an exact expected information gives an exact one here. The density, the distribution function, the quantile function, the generator and the response derivatives are the parent's at the mapped parameters.

The density, the distribution function, the quantile function and the generator call the map once per evaluation, on whole vectors. When map_derivs is NULL, the derivatives call the map at the points of the stencil, several times for each observation (more at higher orders), and separately for each observation when a parameter varies by observation. A supplied map_derivs is called once per evaluation.

See also

fixed(), transformation()

Examples

# This is a gaussian in its mean and variance, obtained rather than written.
d <- reparametrize(
  gaussian1_distrib(),
  map = function(psi) list(mu = psi$mu, sigma = sqrt(psi$sigma2)),
  params = c("mu", "sigma2"),
  bounds = list(mu = c(-Inf, Inf), sigma2 = c(0, Inf)),
  links = list(mu = linkfunctions7::identity_link(),
               sigma2 = linkfunctions7::log_link())
)
theta <- list(mu = 1, sigma2 = 4)
distrib_pdf(d, c(0, 1, 2), theta)
#> [1] 0.1760327 0.1994711 0.1760327

# and it agrees with the family written out by hand
distrib_pdf(gaussian2_distrib(), c(0, 1, 2), theta)
#> [1] 0.1760327 0.1994711 0.1760327
